comment: Each public claim, where it is stated, and the evidence behind it. tests/test_claims_ledger.py fails if a claim's text disappears from its file, if a named test no longer exists, or if a banned phrase appears in the README or docs. 'verified' needs evidence; 'limitation' is something we say we do not do or know; an external claim lives outside this repository and is only listed.

claims.claim: Exactly four tools for an AI agent
None of them can approve, apply, stop or change a limit
approvals bound to
a stop that needs no approval
loopback by default
refuses DTDs and entities
These adapters are observe-only
Status: pre-alpha. Simulation only.
claims.note: Only simulated adapters are accepted by the Bridge; no hardware adapter exists.

claims.claim: If a workspace is set and the adapter cannot report positions, everything is refused
Nothing here controls real hardware
claims.note: An absence claim: backed by the Bridge refusing non-simulated adapters, not by a search of all code.

claims.claim: exact replay within one installed environment
claims.note: Within one environment only. See C11.

claims.claim: cross-machine repeatability is not claimed
claims.note: Not measured. A comparison across MuJoCo 3.17.0 and 4.0.0 is planned (issue 1130) and would still be two environments, not two machines.

claims.claim: not reviewed by native speakers
claims.note: Translations are drafts that no second native speaker has read. Review calls: issues 1122, 1123 and 1281.

claims.claim: out-of-range
the AI can only adjust a tool offset
claims.note: The only command is set_tool_offset; the numbers in the machine-tool model are invented (see C15).

claims.claim: the wear-study numbers are invented
claims.note: External text (the project wiki), listed so that it is not forgotten.

claims.claim: 604 passed, 16 skipped (designed skips)
claims.where: wiki: Home.md and Roadmap.md, ragleap-physical rows

evidence.ref: Colab 2026-11-07, Python 3.13.18, pytest 8.4.2, MuJoCo 4.0.0, MCP SDK 1.30.0; run from the TestPyPI source archive of 0.0.5

claims.note: External text. The 16 skips are the control-only cases of four observe-only adapters, by design.

claims.claim: Not independently audited
claims.where: wiki: Home.md and Roadmap.md, ragleap-physical rows
claims.note: External text. The English README does not say it; the wiki does.

claims.claim: compared after Unicode NFKC normalisation and case folding
claims.note: Fixed in PR 1340 (issue 1337). Deliberate break checked: restoring the exact-text comparison fails the test. REAL, 2026-11-11, simulation only.

claims.claim: The stop flag is now checked again right before the first adapter call
claims.note: PR 1340 (issue 1339). Narrowed, not closed: see the next row. Deliberate break checked. REAL, 2026-11-11.

claims.claim: it does not close it for a stop from another thread that lands between the check and the call
claims.note: A full answer needs adapters to refuse commands while stopped. Issue 1339 stays open.

claims.claim: read and discard what the client still sends, for at most 0.5 s and 1 MiB
claims.note: PR 1341 (issue 1336). Checked on Linux only: five deliberate breaks caught. REAL, 2026-11-11. This row says nothing about Windows.

claims.claim: It has not been run by the project on Windows and has not been repeated by anyone else
claims.note: Linux keeps the answer after the close, so it cannot show the symptom. One volunteer's run on Windows 11 with Python 3.11.4, reported in issue 1114: the commit before the change (e22693e) failed 9 of 50 iterations, the commit with it (99c47b1) 0 of 50. The two commits differ only by this change. A single machine and a single Python version; which test failed and the error text were asked for in the thread.

claims.claim: the console failure a Windows tester saw is not explained by it
claims.note: The console path drains small bodies, so the oversize-body cause does not explain it. Open.

claims.claim: The 0.0.3 refusal fix was not enough.
claims.note: A Windows tester still saw WinError 10053 on 0.0.3 and 0.0.5.

claims.claim: refuse `apply()` with `ValueError` while stopped and change nothing
claims.note: PR for issue 1339. Checked on the simulated stand-ins and the MuJoCo servo adapter; before the change four stand-ins and the three MuJoCo servo cases failed this test. REAL, 2026-11-11. Says nothing about real devices.

claims.claim: A stop now invalidates every approval given before it
claims.note: Option A of issue 1338, merged by the maintainer's decision. Deliberate breaks checked. REAL. Simulated adapters only.

claims.claim: A seeded red-team harness (`benchmarks/redteam/`) sends generated hostile cases through the bridge, the four tools, the MCP server and the console, in simulation only, and reports any case that gets through.
claims.note: REAL, 2026-11-17, Python 3.10.12, main at bb591ced, simulation only: seeds 1 to 3 with 100 cases per class, nothing got through, 0 unclean refusals, 0 errors (about 2,100 cases per seed); 35 deliberate one-line breaks of the library were all reported (benchmarks/redteam/breakcheck_redteam.py). No finding is not a proof that nothing can get through. Says nothing about real devices.

claims.claim: The red-team harness does not cover S6, S11, S12 and S13, and it watches S3 only indirectly.
claims.note: The class-to-invariant mapping (benchmarks/redteam/invariants.json) is a hand-made reading of docs/safety-invariants.md, not a proof of coverage.

claims.claim: The CSV replay adapter is observe-only: it has no command and no write path
claims.note: Every limit and check of the adapter has a deliberate-break row; rows where a second guard refuses the same input are reported as equivalent. REAL. Simulated adapter only; no real file of a third-party dataset was used.

claims.claim: Each file is at most 5,000,000 bytes, 100,000 data rows and 64 header cells
claims.note: The caps are hard: a caller may ask for lower byte and row caps, never for higher ones. Deliberate breaks checked. REAL.

claims.claim: It has not been run on a real file of that dataset, and no claim is made that it works with that data
claims.note: The milling signal description is built from the signal table of a data paper and is marked [unverified]; its ranges are loose sanity bounds chosen here.

claims.claim: A stop request is answered while an apply is still running and behind a client that never finishes its request
claims.note: Issue 1367. REAL, 2026-11-22, Python 3.10.12, loopback, simulated adapters only. Deliberate breaks checked: not threaded, no lock on the counters, no connection cap, busy answer not counted. Says nothing about real devices or about the MCP server.

claims.claim: The MCP server still serves one request at a time; it has no stop tool
claims.note: The MCP server has no stop tool (S10), so a stalled client there delays other tool calls only.

claims.claim: a local client that holds every slot can still delay a stop for up to the read timeout
claims.note: At most 32 connections; the next one is refused with 503 at once. The read timeout is 5 s.
